paragraphs.text: And there are gathered together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, who had come from Jerusalem,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ συνάγονται πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καί τινες τῶν γραμματέων ἐλθόντες ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων
paragraphs.translit: Kai synagontai pros auton hoi Pharisaioi kai tines tōn grammateōn elthontes apo Hierosolymōn

paragraphs.text: and had seen that some of his disciples ate their bread with defiled, that is, unwashen, hands.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδόντες τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὅτι κοιναῖς χερσίν, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν ἀνίπτοις, ἐσθίουσιν τοὺς ἄρτους—
paragraphs.translit: kai idontes tinas tōn mathētōn autou hoti koinais chersin, toutʼ estin aniptois, esthiousin tous artous—

paragraphs.text: (For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, except they wash their hands diligently, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders;
paragraphs.original: οἱ γὰρ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ πάντες οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐὰν μὴ πυγμῇ νίψωνται τὰς χεῖρας οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν, κρατοῦντες τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων,
paragraphs.translit: hoi gar Pharisaioi kai pantes hoi Ioudaioi ean mē pygmē nipsōntai tas cheiras ouk esthiousin, kratountes tēn paradosin tōn presbyterōn,

paragraphs.text: and [when they come] from the market-place, except they bathe themselves, they eat not; and many other things there are, which they have received to hold, washings of cups, and pots, and brasen vessels.)
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπʼ ἀγορᾶς ἐὰν μὴ βαπτίσωνται οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν, καὶ ἄλλα πολλά ἐστιν ἃ παρέλαβον κρατεῖν, βαπτισμοὺς ποτηρίων καὶ ξεστῶν καὶ χαλκίων καὶ κλινῶν—
paragraphs.translit: kai apʼ agoras ean mē baptisōntai ouk esthiousin, kai alla polla estin ha parelabon kratein, baptismous potēriōn kai xestōn kai chalkiōn kai klinōn—

paragraphs.text: And the Pharisees and the scribes ask him, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat their bread with defiled hands?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπερωτῶσιν αὐτὸν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς· Διὰ τί οὐ περιπατοῦσιν οἱ μαθηταί σου κατὰ τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων, ἀλλὰ κοιναῖς χερσὶν ἐσθίουσιν τὸν ἄρτον;
paragraphs.translit: kai eperōtōsin auton hoi Pharisaioi kai hoi grammateis· Dia ti ou peripatousin hoi mathētai sou kata tēn paradosin tōn presbyterōn, alla koinais chersin esthiousin ton arton;

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoreth me with their lips, But their heart is far from me.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Καλῶς ἐπροφήτευσεν Ἠσαΐας περὶ ὑμῶν τῶν ὑποκριτῶν, ὡς γέγραπται ὅτι Οὗτος ὁ λαὸς τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἀπέχει ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autois· Kalōs eprophēteusen Ēsaias peri hymōn tōn hypokritōn, hōs gegraptai hoti Houtos ho laos tois cheilesin me tima, hē de kardia autōn porrō apechei apʼ emou·

paragraphs.text: But in vain do they worship me, Teaching [as their] doctrines the precepts of men.
paragraphs.original: μάτην δὲ σέβονταί με, διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων·
paragraphs.translit: matēn de sebontai me, didaskontes didaskalias entalmata anthrōpōn·

paragraphs.text: Ye leave the commandment of God, and hold fast the tradition of men.
paragraphs.original: ἀφέντες τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ θεοῦ κρατεῖτε τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
paragraphs.translit: aphentes tēn entolēn tou theou krateite tēn paradosin tōn anthrōpōn.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Full well do ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your tradition.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Καλῶς ἀθετεῖτε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν τηρήσητε·
paragraphs.translit: Kai elegen autois· Kalōs atheteite tēn entolēn tou theou, hina tēn paradosin hymōn tērēsēte·

paragraphs.text: For Moses said, Honor thy father and thy mother; and, He that speaketh evil of father or mother, let him die the death:
paragraphs.original: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ εἶπεν· Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα σου, καί· Ὁ κακολογῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα θανάτῳ τελευτάτω·
paragraphs.translit: Mōysēs gar eipen· Tima ton patera sou kai tēn mētera sou, kai· Ho kakologōn patera ē mētera thanatō teleutatō·

paragraphs.text: but ye say, If a man shall say to his father or his mother, That wherewith thou mightest have been profited by me is Corban, that is to say, Given [to God];
paragraphs.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ λέγετε· Ἐὰν εἴπῃ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί· Κορβᾶν, ὅ ἐστιν Δῶρον, ὃ ἐὰν ἐξ ἐμοῦ ὠφεληθῇς,
paragraphs.translit: hymeis de legete· Ean eipē anthrōpos tō patri ē tē mētri· Korban, ho estin Dōron, ho ean ex emou ōphelēthēs,

paragraphs.text: ye no longer suffer him to do aught for his father or his mother;
paragraphs.original: οὐκέτι ἀφίετε αὐτὸν οὐδὲν ποιῆσαι τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί,
paragraphs.translit: ouketi aphiete auton ouden poiēsai tō patri ē tē mētri,

paragraphs.text: making void the word of God by your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things ye do.
paragraphs.original: ἀκυροῦντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ τῇ παραδόσει ὑμῶν ᾗ παρεδώκατε· καὶ παρόμοια τοιαῦτα πολλὰ ποιεῖτε.
paragraphs.translit: akyrountes ton logon tou theou tē paradosei hymōn hē paredōkate· kai paromoia toiauta polla poieite.

paragraphs.text: And he called to him the multitude again, and said unto them, Hear me all of you, and understand:
paragraphs.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος πάλιν τὸν ὄχλον ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀκούσατέ μου πάντες καὶ σύνετε.
paragraphs.translit: Kai proskalesamenos palin ton ochlon elegen autois· Akousate mou pantes kai synete.

paragraphs.text: there is nothing from without the man, that going into him can defile him; but the things which proceed out of the man are those that defile the man.
paragraphs.original: οὐδέν ἐστιν ἔξωθεν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς αὐτὸν ὃ δύναται κοινῶσαι αὐτόν· ἀλλὰ τὰ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκπορευόμενά ἐστιν τὰ κοινοῦντα τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
paragraphs.translit: ouden estin exōthen tou anthrōpou eisporeuomenon eis auton ho dynatai koinōsai auton· alla ta ek tou anthrōpou ekporeuomena estin ta koinounta ton anthrōpon.

paragraphs.text: [If any man hath ears to hear, let him hear.]
And when he was entered into the house from the multitude, his disciples asked of him the parable.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὅτε εἰσῆλθεν εἰς οἶκον ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου, ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ τὴν παραβολήν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hote eisēlthen eis oikon apo tou ochlou, epērōtōn auton hoi mathētai autou tēn parabolēn.

paragraphs.text: And he saith unto them, Are ye so without understanding also? Perceive ye not, that whatsoever from without goeth into the man, [it] cannot defile him;
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀσύνετοί ἐστε; οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι πᾶν τὸ ἔξωθεν εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς τὸν ἄνθρωπον οὐ δύναται αὐτὸν κοινῶσαι,
paragraphs.translit: kai legei autois· Houtōs kai hymeis asynetoi este; ou noeite hoti pan to exōthen eisporeuomenon eis ton anthrōpon ou dynatai auton koinōsai,

paragraphs.text: because it goeth not into his heart, but into his belly, and goeth out into the draught? [This he said], making all meats clean.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι οὐκ εἰσπορεύεται αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν καρδίαν ἀλλʼ εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν, καὶ εἰς τὸν ἀφεδρῶνα ἐκπορεύεται;— καθαρίζων πάντα τὰ βρώματα.
paragraphs.translit: hoti ouk eisporeuetai autou eis tēn kardian allʼ eis tēn koilian, kai eis ton aphedrōna ekporeuetai;— katharizōn panta ta brōmata.

paragraphs.text: And he said, That which proceedeth out of the man, that defileth the man.
paragraphs.original: ἔλεγεν δὲ ὅτι Τὸ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκεῖνο κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον·
paragraphs.translit: elegen de hoti To ek tou anthrōpou ekporeuomenon ekeino koinoi ton anthrōpon·

paragraphs.text: For from within, out of the heart of men, evil thoughts proceed, fornications, thefts, murders, adulteries,
paragraphs.original: ἔσωθεν γὰρ ἐκ τῆς καρδίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων οἱ διαλογισμοὶ οἱ κακοὶ ἐκπορεύονται, πορνεῖαι, κλοπαί, φόνοι,
paragraphs.translit: esōthen gar ek tēs kardias tōn anthrōpōn hoi dialogismoi hoi kakoi ekporeuontai, porneiai, klopai, phonoi,

paragraphs.text: covetings, wickednesses, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, railing, pride, foolishness:
paragraphs.original: μοιχεῖαι, πλεονεξίαι, πονηρίαι, δόλος, ἀσέλγεια, ὀφθαλμὸς πονηρός, βλασφημία, ὑπερηφανία, ἀφροσύνη·
paragraphs.translit: moicheiai, pleonexiai, ponēriai, dolos, aselgeia, ophthalmos ponēros, blasphēmia, hyperēphania, aphrosynē·

paragraphs.text: all these evil things proceed from within, and defile the man.
paragraphs.original: πάντα ταῦτα τὰ πονηρὰ ἔσωθεν ἐκπορεύεται καὶ κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
paragraphs.translit: panta tauta ta ponēra esōthen ekporeuetai kai koinoi ton anthrōpon.

paragraphs.text: And from thence he arose, and went away into the borders of Tyre and Sidon. And he entered into a house, and would have no man know it; and he could not be hid.
paragraphs.original: Ἐκεῖθεν δὲ ἀναστὰς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια Τύρου. καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς οἰκίαν οὐδένα ἤθελεν γνῶναι, καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθη λαθεῖν·
paragraphs.translit: Ekeithen de anastas apēlthen eis ta horia Tyrou. kai eiselthōn eis oikian oudena ēthelen gnōnai, kai ouk ēdynēthē lathein·

paragraphs.text: But straightway a woman, whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having heard of him, came and fell down at his feet.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ εὐθὺς ἀκούσασα γυνὴ περὶ αὐτοῦ, ἧς εἶχεν τὸ θυγάτριον αὐτῆς πνεῦμα ἀκάθαρτον, ἐλθοῦσα προσέπεσεν πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: allʼ euthys akousasa gynē peri autou, hēs eichen to thygatrion autēs pneuma akatharton, elthousa prosepesen pros tous podas autou·

paragraphs.text: Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by race. And she besought him that he would cast forth the demon out of her daughter.
paragraphs.original: ἡ δὲ γυνὴ ἦν Ἑλληνίς, Συροφοινίκισσα τῷ γένει· καὶ ἠρώτα αὐτὸν ἵνα τὸ δαιμόνιον ἐκβάλῃ ἐκ τῆς θυγατρὸς αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: hē de gynē ēn Hellēnis, Syrophoinikissa tō genei· kai ērōta auton hina to daimonion ekbalē ek tēs thygatros autēs.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children`s bread and cast it to the dogs.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτῇ· Ἄφες πρῶτον χορτασθῆναι τὰ τέκνα, οὐ γὰρ καλόν ἐστιν λαβεῖν τὸν ἄρτον τῶν τέκνων καὶ τοῖς κυναρίοις βαλεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: kai elegen autē· Aphes prōton chortasthēnai ta tekna, ou gar kalon estin labein ton arton tōn teknōn kai tois kynariois balein.

paragraphs.text: But she answered and saith unto him, Yea, Lord; even the dogs under the table eat of the children`s crumbs.
paragraphs.original: ἡ δὲ ἀπεκρίθη καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Κύριε, καὶ τὰ κυνάρια ὑποκάτω τῆς τραπέζης ἐσθίουσιν ἀπὸ τῶν ψιχίων τῶν παιδίων.
paragraphs.translit: hē de apekrithē kai legei autō· Kyrie, kai ta kynaria hypokatō tēs trapezēs esthiousin apo tōn psichiōn tōn paidiōn.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto her, For this saying go thy way; the demon is gone out of thy daughter.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Διὰ τοῦτον τὸν λόγον ὕπαγε, ἐξελήλυθεν ἐκ τῆς θυγατρός σου τὸ δαιμόνιον.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autē· Dia touton ton logon hypage, exelēlythen ek tēs thygatros sou to daimonion.

paragraphs.text: And she went away unto her house, and found the child laid upon the bed, and the demon gone out.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπελθοῦσα εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτῆς εὗρεν τὸ παιδίον βεβλημένον ἐπὶ τὴν κλίνην καὶ τὸ δαιμόνιον ἐξεληλυθός.
paragraphs.translit: kai apelthousa eis ton oikon autēs heuren to paidion beblēmenon epi tēn klinēn kai to daimonion exelēlythos.

paragraphs.text: And again he went out from the borders of Tyre, and came through Sidon unto the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the borders of Decapolis.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ πάλιν ἐξελθὼν ἐκ τῶν ὁρίων Τύρου ἦλθεν διὰ Σιδῶνος εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν ὁρίων Δεκαπόλεως.
paragraphs.translit: Kai palin exelthōn ek tōn horiōn Tyrou ēlthen dia Sidōnos eis tēn thalassan tēs Galilaias ana meson tōn horiōn Dekapoleōs.

paragraphs.text: And they bring unto him one that was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech; and they beseech him to lay his hand upon him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτῷ κωφὸν καὶ μογιλάλον, καὶ παρακαλοῦσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιθῇ αὐτῷ τὴν χεῖρα.
paragraphs.translit: kai pherousin autō kōphon kai mogilalon, kai parakalousin auton hina epithē autō tēn cheira.

paragraphs.text: And he took him aside from the multitude privately, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spat, and touched his tongue;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπολαβόμενος αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου κατʼ ἰδίαν ἔβαλεν τοὺς δακτύλους αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰ ὦτα αὐτοῦ καὶ πτύσας ἥψατο τῆς γλώσσης αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: kai apolabomenos auton apo tou ochlou katʼ idian ebalen tous daktylous autou eis ta ōta autou kai ptysas hēpsato tēs glōssēs autou,

paragraphs.text: and looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἐστέναξεν, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Εφφαθα, ὅ ἐστιν Διανοίχθητι·
paragraphs.translit: kai anablepsas eis ton ouranon estenaxen, kai legei autō· Ephphatha, ho estin Dianoichthēti·

paragraphs.text: And his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἠνοίγησαν αὐτοῦ αἱ ἀκοαί, καὶ ἐλύθη ὁ δεσμὸς τῆς γλώσσης αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐλάλει ὀρθῶς·
paragraphs.translit: kai ēnoigēsan autou hai akoai, kai elythē ho desmos tēs glōssēs autou, kai elalei orthōs·

paragraphs.text: And he charged them that they should tell no man: but the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal they published it.
paragraphs.original: καὶ διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ λέγωσιν· ὅσον δὲ αὐτοῖς διεστέλλετο, αὐτοὶ μᾶλλον περισσότερον ἐκήρυσσον.
paragraphs.translit: kai diesteilato autois hina mēdeni legōsin· hoson de autois diestelleto, autoi mallon perissoteron ekērysson.

paragraphs.text: And they were beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things well; he maketh even the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὑπερπερισσῶς ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες· Καλῶς πάντα πεποίηκεν, καὶ τοὺς κωφοὺς ποιεῖ ἀκούειν καὶ ἀλάλους λαλεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hyperperissōs exeplēssonto legontes· Kalōs panta pepoiēken, kai tous kōphous poiei akouein kai alalous lalein.
